The following objection therefore does not arise: if the principle were true, every material individual, such as a human individual, would have to attain the utmost intellectual and imaginative perfection proper to it, because this is nobler than its potential existence, whereas most individuals are deprived of their final perfection and barred from their ultimate existence.

notes.text: “The principle of the possibility of the nobler” renders qāʿidat imkān al-ashraf. The chapter distinguishes the principle itself from the stronger claim that every material species must have a separate archetype of the same specific quiddity.

units.arabicTitle: الفصل الحادي والعشرون — في عالم المثال
units.arabic:
ويسمّى أيضاً «البرزخ» ، لتوسّطه بين العالم العقليّ وعالم المادّة والطبيعة. وهو ـ كما ظهر ممّا تقدّم ـ مرتبةٌ من الوجود مجرّدةٌ عن المادّة دون آثارها من

الكم والكيف والوضع ونحوها من الأعراض ، والعلّة الموجِدة له هو آخر العقول الطوليّة المسمّى «عقلا فعّالا» عند المشّائين ، و «بعض العقول العرضيّة» عند الإشراقيّين .

وفيه أمثلة الصور الجوهريّة التي هي جهات الكثرة في العقل المفيض لهذا العالم المتمثّل بعضها لبعض بهيئات مختلفة من غير أن يفسد اختلاف الهيئات الوحدةَ الشخصيّةَ التي لجوهره. مثال ذلك : أنّ جمعاً كثيراً من أفراد الإنسان ـ مثلا ـ يتصوّرون بعض من لم يروه من الماضين ، وإنّما سمعوا اسمه وشيئاً من سيرته ، كلّ منهم يمثّله في نفسه بهيأة مناسبة لما يقدّره عليه بما عنده من صفته وإن غايرت الهيأة التي له عند غيره.

ولهذه النكتة قسموا المثالَ إلى خيال منفصل قائم بنفسه مستقلٍّ عن النفوس الجزئيّة المتخيّلة وخيال متّصل قائم بالنفوس الجزئيّة المتخيّلة.

على أنّ في متخيّلات النفوس صوراً جزافيّةً لا تناسب فعلَ الحكيم ، وفيها نسبةٌ إلى دعابات المتخيّلة.
units.title: The imaginal realm
units.english:
It is also called the “intermediate realm,” because it lies between the intellectual realm and the realm of matter and nature. As became clear from the foregoing, it is a degree of existence free of matter but not of matter’s effects, such as quantity, quality, position, and similar accidents. The cause bringing it into existence is the last of the vertical intellects, called the “Agent Intellect” by the Peripatetics, or some of the horizontal intellects according to the Illuminationists.

It contains the images of substantial forms that are aspects of multiplicity in the intellect bestowing this realm. Some are presented to others in different configurations, without the differences of configuration impairing the individual unity of the substance concerned. An example is that many human individuals conceive someone from the past whom they have not seen, but whose name and something of whose life they have heard. Each represents him within himself in a configuration appropriate to what he supposes him to be, according to the attributes he knows, even if this differs from the configuration that person has for someone else.

Because of this point, they have divided the imaginal into separate imagination, subsisting in its own right independently of particular imagining souls, and connected imagination, subsisting in particular imagining souls.

Moreover, among the things imagined by souls are arbitrary forms that do not befit the act of a wise agent and bear a relation to the play of the imaginative faculty.

units.arabicTitle: الفصل الثاني والعشرون — في العالم الماديّ
units.arabic:
وهو العالم المحسوس أخسّ مراتب الوجود ، ويتميّز عن العالميَنْ ـ عالم العقل وعالم المثال ـ بتعلُّقِ الصور فيه ذاتاً وفعلا أو فعلا بالمادّة وتوقّفها على الاستعداد. فما للأنواع التي فيها من الكمالات هي في أوّل الوجود بالقوّة ، ثمّ يخرج إلى الفعليّة بالتدريج ، وربّما عاقها من كمالها عائق ، فالعلل فيها متزاحمة متمانعة.

وقد عثرَتْ الأبحاث العلميّة الطبيعيّة والرياضيّة إلى هذه الأيّام على شيء

كثير من أجزاء هذا العالم والنسب التي بينها والنظام الجاري فيها. ولعلّ ما هو مجهول منها أكثر ممّا هو معلوم.

وقد تبيّن في الأبحاث السابقة أنّ عالم المادّة بما بين أجزائه من الارتباط والاتّصال واحدٌ سيّالٌ في ذاته متحرّكٌ في جوهره ويشايعه في ذلك الأعراض ، والغاية التي تنتهي إليها هذه الحركة العامّة هي التجرّد على ما تقدّمت الإشارة إليه في مرحلة القوّة والفعل .

وإذ كان هذا العالم حركةً ومتحرّكاً في جوهره ، سيلاناً وسيّالا في وجوده ، وكانت هويّته عين التجدّد والتغيّر لا شيئاً يطرأ عليه التجدّد والتغيّر ، صحّ ارتباطه بالعلّة الثابتة التي تَنَزَّه عن التجدّد والتغيّر.

فالجاعل الثابت الوجود جَعَلَ ما هو في ذاته متجدّدٌ متغيّرٌ ، لا أنّه جَعَل الشيء متجدّداً متغيّراً. وبذلك يرتفع إشكال استناد المتغيّر إلى الثابت وارتباط الحادث بالقديم.
units.title: The material realm
units.english:
This is the sensible realm, the lowest degree of existence. It is distinguished from the other two realms—the intellectual and imaginal—by its forms being attached to matter in both essence and act, or in act, and by their dependence upon preparedness. The perfections belonging to its species are potential at the beginning of existence and then gradually become actual. An obstacle may prevent them from attaining their perfection, so causes within it compete and obstruct one another.

Down to the present day, natural and mathematical investigations have discovered much about the parts of this realm, the relations between them, and the order prevailing among them. Perhaps what remains unknown is greater than what is known.

It became clear in the preceding discussions that the material realm, through the connections and continuity among its parts, is one, flowing in its essence and moving in its substance, with accidents accompanying it in this. The end at which this universal motion terminates is immateriality, as indicated in the stage on potentiality and actuality.

Since this realm is motion and moving in its substance, flow and flowing in its existence, and since its identity is renewal and change themselves rather than something upon which renewal and change supervene, its connection to an immutable cause, free of renewal and change, is valid.

The maker whose existence is immutable makes that which is intrinsically renewed and changing; it does not make a thing become renewed and changing. In this way the difficulty of the changing depending upon the immutable, and of the originated being connected to the eternal, is removed.

units.arabicTitle: الفصل الثالث والعشرون — في حدوث العالم
units.arabic:
قد تحقّق فيما تقدّم من مباحث القدم والحدوث أنّ كلَّ ماهيّة ممكنة موجودة مسبوقةُ الوجود بعدم ذاتيٍّ ، فهي حادثةٌ حدوثاً ذاتيّاً ، والعدم السابق على وجودها بحدّه منتزَعٌ عن علّتها الموجِدة لها ، فهي مسبوقةُ الوجود بوجودِ علِّتها متأخّرةٌ عنها.

وإذ كان المبدأ الأوّل لكلِّ وجود إمكانيٍّ ـ سواء كان مادّياً أو مجرّداً ، عقليّاً أو غير عقليّ ـ هو الواجب لذاته (تعالى) ، فكلُّ ممكن موجود حادثٌ ذاتاً بالنسبة

إليه ، ومجموع الممكنات المسمّى بعالم الإمكان وبما سوى البارئ (تعالى) ليس شيئاً وراء أجزائه ، فحكمه حكم أجزائه ، فالعالم بجميع أجزائه حادثٌ ذاتاً مسبوقُ الوجود بوجود الواجب لذاته.

ثمّ إنّا لو أغمضنا عن الماهيّات وقصرنا النظر في الوجود بما أنّه الحقيقة الأصيلة ، وجدنا الوجود منقسماً إلى واجب لذاته قائم بذاته مستقلٍّ في تحقّقه وثبوته وممكن موجود في غيره رابط قائم بغيره الذي هو الواجب ، كان كلّ وجود إمكانيّ مسبوقاً بالوجود الواجبيّ حادثاً هذا النحو من الحدوث ، وحكم مجموع الوجودات الإمكانيّة حكم أجزائه ، فالمجموع حادث بحدوثه.

ثمّ إنّ لعالم المادّة والطبيعة حدوثاً آخر يخصّه وهو الحدوث الزمانيّ. تقريره : أنّه قد تقدّم في مباحث القوّة والفعل أنّ عالم المادّة متحرّكٌ بجوهره وما يلحق به من الأعراض ، سيّالٌ وجوداً ، متجدّدٌ بالهويّة ، سالكٌ بذاته من النقص إلى الكمال ، متحوّلٌ من القوّة ، منقسمٌ إلى حدود ، كلّ حدّ منها فعليّةٌ لسابقه قوّةٌ للاحقه ، ثمّ لو قسم هذا الحدّ بعينه كان كلّما حدث بالانقسام حدّ كان فعليّةً لسابقه قوّةً للاحقه.

وإنّ هذه الحركة العامّة ترسم امتداداً كميّاً كلّما فرض منه قطعة انقسمت إلى قبلُ وبعدُ ، وكذا كلّ قبلُ منه وبعدُ ينقسمان إلى قبلُ وبعدُ ، من غير وقوف على حدّ ما ذكر في الحركة التي ترسمه؛ وإنّما الفرق بين الإمتدادَيْن أنّ الذي للحركة مبهمٌ والذي لهذا الامتداد العارض لها متعيّن ، نظير الفرق بين الجسم الطبيعيّ والجسم التعليميّ.

وهذا الامتداد الذي يرسمه جوهر العالم بحركته هو الزمان العامّ الذي به تتقدّر الحركات وتتعيّن النسب بين الحوادث الطبيعيّة بالطول والقصر والقبليّة والبعديّة ، وقبليّته هي كونه قوّةً للفعليّة التي تليه ، وبعديّته هي كونه فعليّةً للقوّة التي تليه.

فكلّ قطعة من قطعات هذه الحركة العامّة الممتدّة أخذناها ، وجدناها مسبوقةً بعدم زمانيّ ، لكونها فعليّة مسبوقة بقوّة ، فهي حادثة بحدوث زمانيّ. ومجموع هذه

القطعات والأجزاء ليس إلاّ نفس القطعات والأجزاء ، فحكمه حكمها ، وهو حادثٌ زمانيٌّ بحدوثها الزمانيّ ، فعالم المادّة والطبيعة حادثٌ حدوثاً زمانيّاً ، هذا.

وأمّا ما صوّره المتكلّمون في حدوث العالم ـ يعني ما سوى البارئ سبحانه ـ زماناً بالبناء على استحالة القدم الزمانيّ في الممكن. ومحصّله : أنّ الوجودات الإمكانيّة منقطعة من طرف البداية ، فلا موجود قبلها إلاّ الواجب (تعالى) ، والزمان ذاهبٌ من الجانبَيْن إلى غير النهاية ، وصدره خال عن العالم ، وذيله مشغول به ظرف له.

ففيه : أنّ الزمان نفسه موجود ممكن مخلوق للواجب (تعالى) ، فليجعل من العالم الذي هو فعله (تعالى) ، وعند ذاك ليس وراء الواجب وفعله أمر آخر ، فلا قبل حتّى يستقرّ فيه عدم العالم إستقرارَ المظروف في ظرفه؛ على أنّ القول بلا تناهي الزمان أوّلا وآخراً يناقض قولَهم باستحالة القديم الزمانيّ؛ مضافاً إلى أنّ الزمان كمٌّ عارضٌ للحركة القائمة بالجسم ، وعدم تناهيه يلازم عدمَ تناهي الأجسام وحركاتها ، وهو قدم العالم المناقض لقولهم بحدوثه.

وقد تفصّى بعضهم عن إشكال لزوم كون الزمان لا واجباً ولا معلولا للواجب بأنّ الزمان أمر إعتباريّ لا بأس بالقول بكونه لا واجباً ولا معلولا للواجب.

وفيه : أنّه يستوي حينئذ القول بحدوث العالم وقدمه زماناً ، إذ لا حقيقة للزمان.

وتفصّى عنه آخرون بأنّ الزمان إنتزاعيٌّ منتزَعٌ من الوجود الواجبيّ تعالى

عن ذلك.

واعتُرِض عليه : بأنّ لازمه عروض التغيّر للذات الواجبيّة.

واُجيب عنه : بأنّا لا نسلّم وجوب المطابقة بين المنتزع والمنتزع عنه. وأنت خبير بأنّه التزام بالسفسطة.
units.title: The origination of the world
units.english:
It was established in the preceding discussions of eternity and origination that every existent contingent quiddity is preceded in existence by intrinsic nonexistence. It is therefore intrinsically originated. The nonexistence preceding its existence in its particular limit is abstracted from its cause that brings it into existence. Its existence is thus preceded by the existence of its cause and posterior to it.

Since the first principle of every contingent existence—whether material or immaterial, intellectual or otherwise—is the intrinsically Necessary—exalted is He—every contingent existent is intrinsically originated in relation to Him. The aggregate of contingent things, called the contingent world and everything other than the Creator, is nothing beyond its parts. Its ruling is therefore the ruling of its parts. The world with all its parts is intrinsically originated, its existence preceded by the existence of the intrinsically Necessary.

If we then disregard quiddities and confine our consideration to existence as the fundamental reality, we find existence divided into what is intrinsically necessary, subsisting through itself and independent in its realization and establishment, and what is contingent, existing in another, relational, and subsisting through another, namely the Necessary. Every contingent existence is therefore preceded by necessary existence and originated through this kind of origination. The ruling of the aggregate of contingent existences is the ruling of its parts, so the aggregate is originated through their origination.

The world of matter and nature has another origination peculiar to it: temporal origination. Its account is as follows. It was established in the discussions of potentiality and actuality that the material realm moves in its substance and in the accidents accompanying it. It flows in existence, is renewed in identity, proceeds intrinsically from deficiency to perfection, and passes out of potentiality. It is divisible into limits, each of which is an actuality for what precedes it and a potentiality for what follows it. If that same limit is divided, every limit produced through the division is again an actuality for what precedes it and a potentiality for what follows it.

This universal motion traces a quantitative extension such that every segment supposed within it divides into before and after. Likewise, every before and after divides into before and after, without stopping at any limit, as described for the motion tracing it. The difference between the two extensions is that the extension belonging to motion is indeterminate, whereas this extension occurring to motion is determinate, like the difference between the natural body and the mathematical body.

This extension traced by the substance of the world through its motion is universal time, through which motions are measured and relations among natural events are determined in terms of length, shortness, priority, and posteriority. Its priority is its being potentiality for the actuality adjoining it, and its posteriority is its being actuality for the potentiality adjoining it.

Every segment we take from the segments of this extended universal motion is found to be preceded by temporal nonexistence, because it is an actuality preceded by potentiality. It is therefore temporally originated. The aggregate of these segments and parts is nothing but the segments and parts themselves. Its ruling is therefore theirs, and it is temporally originated through their temporal origination. The world of matter and nature is thus temporally originated.

As for the theologians’ account of the temporal origination of the world—that is, everything other than the Creator, glorified is He—it is based upon the impossibility of temporal eternity for the contingent. Its substance is that contingent existences have a beginning beyond which they do not extend, so that before them no existent is found except the Necessary. Time stretches infinitely in both directions; its earlier portion is empty of the world, while its later portion is occupied by and serves as a receptacle for the world.

The objection is that time itself is a contingent existent created by the Necessary. It must therefore be included in the world that is His act. There is then nothing beyond the Necessary and His act, and no “before” in which the world’s nonexistence could be established as something contained in a receptacle. Moreover, asserting time’s infinity at both beginning and end contradicts their assertion of the impossibility of what is temporally eternal. Furthermore, time is a quantity occurring to motion subsisting in a body. Its infinity necessarily accompanies the infinity of bodies and their motions, which is the eternity of the world and contradicts their claim of its origination.

Some have attempted to escape the difficulty that time would be neither necessary nor an effect of the Necessary by saying that time is something intellectually considered, so there is no objection to saying it is neither necessary nor an effect of the Necessary.

The objection is that asserting the world’s temporal origination and its temporal eternity would then be equivalent, since time would have no reality.

Others have attempted to escape it by saying that time is something abstracted from necessary existence—exalted is He above that.

It was objected that this would entail the occurrence of change in the necessary essence.

The answer offered was: “We do not concede that what is abstracted must correspond to that from which it is abstracted.” You are well aware that this is a commitment to sophistry.

units.arabicTitle: الفصل الرابع والعشرون — في دوام الفيض
units.arabic:
قد تبيّن في الأبحاث السابقة أنّ قدرته (تعالى) هي مبدئيّته للإيجاد وعلّيّته لما سواه ، وهي عين الذات المتعالية ، ولازم ذلك دوام الفيض واستمرار الرحمة وعدم انقطاع العطيّة.

ولا يلزم من ذلك دوام عالم الطبيعة ، لأنّ المجموع ليس شيئاً وراء الأجزاء ، وكلّ جزء حادث مسبوقٌ بالعدم ، ولا تكرُّرَ في وجود العالم على ما يراه القائلون بالأدوار والأكوار ، لعدم الدليل عليه.

وما قيل : «إنّ الأفلاك والأجرام العلويّة دائمة الوجود بأشخاصها ، وكذلك

كلّيّات العناصر والأنواع الأصليّة المادّيّة دائمة الوجود نظراً إلى أنّ عللها مفارقة آبية عن التغيّر».

يدفعه عدم دليل يدلّ على كون هذه العلل تامّةً منحصرةً غيرَ متوقّفة في تأثيرها على شرائط ومتعدّات مجهولة لنا تختلف معلولاتها باختلافها ، فلا تتشابه الخلقة في أدوارها.

على أنّ القول بالأفلاك والأجرام غير القابلة للتغيّر وغير ذلك ، كانت أصولا موضوعة من الهيأة والطبيعيّات القديمتين ، وقد انفسخ اليوم هذه الآراء.

تمّ الكتاب والحمد لله في سادس محرم الحرام من سنة ألف وثلاثمائة وخمس وتسعين من الهجرة النبويّة والصلاة على محمّد وآله.
units.title: The perpetuity of emanation
units.english:
It became clear in the preceding discussions that His power—exalted is He—is His being a principle of bringing into existence and His causality in relation to all else, and that it is identical with the transcendent essence. This necessarily entails the perpetuity of emanation, the continuity of mercy, and the uninterrupted bestowal of gifts.

This does not require the perpetuity of the natural world, because the aggregate is nothing beyond its parts, and every part is originated and preceded by nonexistence. Nor is there repetition in the existence of the world, as held by proponents of cycles and great cycles, since there is no proof for it.

It has been said: “The celestial spheres and higher bodies endure in existence as individuals, and likewise the universals of the elements and the original material species endure in existence, because their causes are separate and do not admit change.”

The reply is that there is no proof that these causes are complete and exclusive, with their influence independent of conditions and preparatory factors unknown to us. Their effects may differ as these conditions differ, so that creation need not be alike in its cycles.

Moreover, the doctrine of celestial spheres and bodies incapable of change, and other such views, were principles taken for granted from ancient astronomy and natural philosophy. These views have now been overturned.

The book was completed, praise be to God, on the sixth of the sacred month of Muḥarram in the year one thousand three hundred and ninety-five of the Prophetic Hijra. Blessings be upon Muḥammad and his family.

glossary.definition: The act or reality of being. Distinguish the concept of existence from the extra-mental reality to which it applies.
That which exists. “Being” can name an existent, so the translation usually reserves “existence” for wujūd.
What a thing is, considered as the answer to “What is it?” Its conceptual distinction from existence is central to the work.
The thesis that existence is primary in concrete realization, while quiddities are abstracted from it. This is an ontological thesis, not a claim that ordinary things are imaginary.
A context-sensitive term. A quiddity’s derivative status, an abstract philosophical concept, and a practical convention should not automatically receive the same English rendering.
Unity of a reality across different degrees, where the basis of difference returns to the basis of agreement. Distinguish this from mere ambiguity of a word.
The intelligible meaning and what it applies to. Distinct concepts need not entail distinct externally existing things.
The domain in relation to which a judgment is true; it should not automatically be reduced to a separate physical object.
Existence whose reality is dependent rather than independently established. Attend to the distinction between a proposition’s copular relation and an effect’s dependence upon its cause.

glossary.english: In itself / for itself / through itself
glossary.definition: Three distinct relations. The translation retains their differences rather than flattening all of them into “independent.”
The mode in which something is present as known without necessarily producing the external effects associated with its extra-mental existence.
The basic modalities. Imkān is “contingency” when contrasted with intrinsic necessity, but “possibility” is preferable in many other modal contexts.
Intrinsic status must be distinguished from status derived from another. A contingent thing can become necessary through its complete cause without becoming intrinsically necessary.
A substance is not in a subject independent of it; an accident exists in such a subject. This distinction does not make accidents unreal.
Matter is the receptive principle and form the actuality through which it is determined. Prime matter is not simply a small physical particle.
Predication considered through identity of meaning or quiddity. Distinguish it from a predication concerning concrete instances.
Predication grounded in unity of instance despite conceptual difference. The literal rendering “industrial predication” is avoided.
The explanatory dependence of an effect upon a cause need not imply that the cause precedes it in time.
The total causal condition upon whose realization the effect necessarily follows. An incomplete cause alone does not suffice for the effect.
Bringing something into existence, distinguished from making an already posited thing possess an additional determination.
A receptive possibility and its realization. Quwwa also means an active power; fiʿl also means an act. The contrast determines the translation.
Change in the existence of material substance itself, rather than only in its accidental states. Its subject and continuity require separate argument.
Two considerations of motion: the moving thing’s state between endpoints, and its successive passage through the course.
Time measures motion. Dahr and sarmad name technical atemporal relations of coexistence. Rendering all three with ordinary temporal language obscures the argument.
Whether existence is or is not preceded by nonexistence. The relevant kind of precedence must be specified; intrinsic origination is not simply a date in the past.
Knowledge in which the known itself is present to the knower, rather than known through a separately mediating acquired form.
Knowledge through the presence of a form representing what is known. “Acquired” here names a mode of knowledge, not necessarily the result of deliberate learning.
Apprehending a meaning and assenting to a judgment. These should be kept distinct when reading the account of acquired knowledge.
The act or principle of intellection, the one knowing, and what is intelligibly known. “Knower” is used where the broader English sense fits the argument.
That whose existence is intrinsically necessary. The final stage argues about its existence, unity, attributes, and acts.
